features.note: Reads unmistakably as a CEILING-MOUNTED mini-dome: flat white base/trim plate up (against the ceiling), smooth bubble hanging BELOW it. The negative-elevation (contrapicado) hero frames the underside where every critical lives — the framing convention accepts a look-up hero for a ceiling subject, as gated at P3. Not built bubble-up (the lazy failure).

THE HARD ONE, solved. The bubble is genuinely transparent and the interior optics are legible THROUGH it in the dome=on hero AND the axial under view — not a milky cap, not an opaque lid, not an empty shell. Transparency is achieved WITHOUT MeshPhysicalMaterial.transmission (which stalls SwiftShader): depthWrite off + DoubleSide + opacity 0.42. The ?dome=off state proves the interior EXISTS rather than being hidden behind a translucent surface — the veil-vs-hole distinction this critical is about, and the exact class as the opaque-lid trap from a prior project.

A distinct lens assembly on a cradle inside the bubble, off-axis and tilted ~22deg, with a dark front element and a retaining ring (an OPEN ring now, not the solid plug that enveloped the lens in an earlier build). Critically, it FACES THE HERO: the builder caught that rotateX(+deg) on a downward axis tilted the optics toward -z while the hero camera sits at +z, so the lens pointed away from the only capture angle. Fixed in GEOMETRY (tilt sign + lens_pan 35deg to the hero azimuth), not by moving the camera to a flattering angle. The conical barrel (30->19mm) no longer self-occludes below the glass on tilt.

A matte black cone fills the bubble interior around the optics, so light through the bubble is absorbed rather than bouncing off a white inner body — which is what stops the camera reading as a ceiling light (plafon). Reads clearly in both dome states.
A visible white trim ring at the base, larger than the bubble (101 vs 79 mm), seating flush against the mounting plane — the collar over the ceiling cutout. 11 mm of collar visible.

important_features.note: A small status indicator reads on the trim ring (unsourced colour/position — confidence 0.6, green convention). Present as a discrete element.
?ceiling=on adds a suspended-ceiling tile prop (scenery, deliberately featureless, correctly EXCLUDED from the subject bbox).

defects: Materials are blockout-basic (the bubble/shroud/body read, but surface refinement — bubble clarity gradient, matte shroud microfacet — is the materials pass).
NOT built (correct): fixing screws — P1 records no count/type/position for a generic unit (same rule as the UPS rear receptacles).
corrections: Structural/materials: refine the bubble's optical read and the lens module detail (front element, retaining ring form).
Lighting pass: keep the below-source rig (this subject's features face down); prove it with the analytic irradiance check; do NOT raise metalness on shroud/barrel to compensate (matte dielectrics).

mechanical.notes: Envelope 0.1010 x 0.0560 x 0.1010 m, exact to spec on all axes. 10 meshes / 4536 tris. Console clean across 4 states (hero dome on/off, under, ceiling). FIVE defects caught+fixed this build, three of the subject-bbox family: (1) Box3.setFromObject IGNORES `visible`, so the 400mm hidden ceiling prop poisoned the bbox to 0.400x0.062x0.400 for a 101mm device — same class as the UPS floating slot, a box describing something other than the object, via a different route; fixed with subjectBox(root) skipping hidden meshes + declared props, used in solveCamera/__qaFraming/checks. (2) four coplanar face pairs seated through surfaces, now seated on. (3) retaining ring was a solid plug enveloping the lens; now an open ring. (4) 30mm straight barrel dropped its rim below the glass on tilt (barrel y=-50.5 vs glass -48.8), blocking the oblique sightline; conical 30->19mm fixes it. (5) THE IMPORTANT ONE: the lens faced AWAY from the hero, caught by a front-face-only visibility check returning 0/43 — a ZERO DENOMINATOR is a different diagnosis than a low score; 'occluded' and 'facing away' only separate under a camera-facing-normal filter (three prior sample definitions averaged them to a plausible 0/18/17%). The tell it was real not a metric artifact: the under (near-axial) view scored 83-100% while the hero scored 0-17% — a part perfect from the state that faces it and near-zero from the delivered state is hiding. Fixed geometry, not the camera. Boot check passes (real main.js: data-app-ready, render loop, 5 buttons, __qaFraming/__qaState callable, solved radii 0.208/0.222 plausible for 101mm not 400mm). Lighting: down-normals 1.715 vs up 0.094 (18.2x) with FOUR lamps below the subject; all critical-bearing normals clear the 0.55 legibility floor; flanks 0.72/0.48; metalness untouched.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. A strong first blockout of the run's hardest asset. Its three genuinely novel problems all landed at once: translucency WITHOUT transmission (depthWrite/DoubleSide/opacity), the veil-vs-hole occlusion (proven by ?dome=off), and the inverted lighting (a below-source rig for downward-facing features, the first in-KIND-different rig answer of the run). The five defects were caught with real rigor — especially the lens-facing-away one, whose zero-denominator visibility signal distinguishes 'occluded' from 'pointed the wrong way', and which was fixed in geometry rather than by tilting the camera to hide it. All five criticals read across the states; the integrity discipline (generic model, split provenance, no fabricated model number, no invented screws) holds and is even surfaced in the PROCEDENCIA HUD. Cleared to the structural pass. Noted separately: the builder's honest UPS coverage-gap flag (__qaFraming was never exercised at boot there; his Axis boot check now exercises it; it works in-browser, which my own UPS captures used) — a coverage gap, not a defect, and it does not change the UPS verdict.
